findings.hypothesis: Each StructuredOutput delta rescans and JSON-parses the entire accumulated text prefix, giving quadratic total work for fixed-size deltas.
findings.whyReachable: Every streamed input_json_delta in a Claude round calls partialText(json), which loops over all text accumulated so far and decodes it again. This is an ordinary streaming path.
findings.expectedScope: Claude structured-output streaming only. Executed real ClaudeProvider.round with fake RPC: 128 x 128-character chunks emitted 16384 correct characters while parsing 1057024 characters; 256 chunks emitted 32768 characters while parsing 4211200. Counts exclude additional regex/loop work. No wall-time or browser CPU gain measured.
findings.risk: Medium implementation risk. Incremental decoding must preserve split backslash/unicode escape handling, text-first schema, monotonic streaming, final output fallback and action boundaries.
findings.cheapReproduction: node build/efficiency-20261103/native-host-probe.mjs; claudeStreaming uses actual round and temporarily counts global JSON.parse input synchronously. No providers.
findings.smallestFix: Keep per-round incremental text extraction state and scan only new JSON characters; emit complete decoded escapes only. Keep final structured_output validation. Alternatively coalesce parsing at a documented small interval while preserving final flush, but measure latency before choosing.
relevantExistingTests: tests/ai/host.test.mjs:294-315 split escapes, streaming and native-tool refusal

findings.hypothesis: The native output writer has no aggregate queue bound or drain handling; slow readers can retain arbitrarily many individually valid encoded frames.
findings.whyReachable: All host replies and provider deltas use send, which ignores stdout.write false. Individual 1 MiB output limit does not cap the Writable queue. JsonLineProcess.send has the same missing pressure handling toward child stdin, but that secondary path was not reproduced.
findings.expectedScope: Host under slow/stalled native output consumption. Exact extracted production send closure plus a blocked Node Writable queued 8394624 bytes for 128 messages with 65536-character payloads despite highWaterMark=1024 and writableNeedDrain=true. Synthetic blocked-reader result; normal Chrome consumption and actual provider rate may keep queues small.
findings.risk: Medium-high. Dropping deltas or tools changes semantics. Queue ownership, bounded admission and orderly cancellation must preserve response order, pending tool replies and error delivery.
findings.cheapReproduction: node build/efficiency-20261103/native-host-probe.mjs; nativeOutput executes unchanged send closure with production encodeMessage and Node Writable. No real pipe or browser used.
findings.smallestFix: Introduce a bounded ordered native writer that waits for drain and stops/cancels request production when its limit is reached. Propagate async admission to producers rather than adding another unbounded JS queue. Validate on a real disposable stdio pipe before implementation approval.

findings.hypothesis: Cancelling a Codex chat during preflight leaves preflight work and isolation alive until the probe finishes or its own timeout fires; rapid cancelled replacements can overlap helpers.
findings.whyReachable: chat awaits isolate/preflight/start before registering abort. preflight has no signal parameter. Controller clears the active run immediately on cancellation, permitting another request while old setup continues.
findings.expectedScope: Actual CodexProvider.chat with injected gated preflight remained unsettled and had not cleaned isolation after abort; releasing preflight produced Cancelled and cleaned up. This proves cancellation ordering only. No real process lifetime, RSS, duration or repeated replacement measured. Real preflight already has request deadlines and a later 15-second receive deadline; it is delayed cleanup, not a permanent leak.
findings.risk: Medium. Cancellation must close only owned probe/runtime/server and remove temporary isolation after process exit, while retaining tool-registry, effort and speed validation for every noncancelled chat.
findings.cheapReproduction: node build/efficiency-20261103/native-host-probe.mjs; codexCancellation overrides isolate/preflight/start and calls real chat with AbortController. Exact next test: fake JsonLineProcess with deferred initialize/thread/start/turn/start at each boundary and assert immediate close, listener cleanup and no later real-chat start.
findings.smallestFix: Pass signal through preflight/start, register abort before setup awaits, check already-aborted signals and await owned process/server cleanup before removing isolation. Do not cache away or skip the security probe.

findings.hypothesis: The response-size guard rejects only after response.text has consumed and assembled the complete body, so it does not bound peak allocation for oversized bodies.
findings.whyReachable: Every successful Organato API response reaches response.text before the 2000000-character check. A timeout limits time, not bytes. An anomalous server response can exceed the intended bound.
findings.expectedScope: Actual Organato.request using fake secrets and a synthetic streaming Response consumed all 4194304 bytes before reporting response too large. This confirms post-consumption enforcement, not occurrence with the real Organato service or ordinary dashboard overhead.
findings.risk: Low-medium. Preserve UTF-8 correctness, cancellation, existing errors, request authorization, no write retries and reasonable legitimate response sizes. Byte and JS-character limits differ.
findings.cheapReproduction: node build/efficiency-20261103/native-host-probe.mjs; organatoResponse supplies Response over a 4 MiB ReadableStream. No config, secrets or network accessed.
findings.smallestFix: Read response.body incrementally with an explicit byte ceiling and cancel its reader at the ceiling; decode/parse only bounded data. Choose the byte policy explicitly while retaining the existing character validation.
relevantExistingTests: tests/ai/organato.test.mjs API contract, invalid credentials and item links; no oversized streaming-response case found

findings.hypothesis: Long JSON lines fragmented into many small chunks may trigger repeated prefix scanning/flattening, even though the line buffer is capped.
findings.whyReachable: Each stdout chunk appends then indexOf scans for newline from the beginning. A long incomplete line revisits its entire prefix until newline arrives.
findings.expectedScope: CLI stdio parsing of large fragmented lines only. Maximum 16 Mi characters bounds retained state; string rope behavior and transport chunk sizes determine copying. No timing/copy-count probe executed.
findings.risk: Medium. Must preserve UTF-8 setEncoding, coalesced lines, pending correlation, parse errors and limits.
findings.cheapReproduction: Next test: instantiate actual JsonLineProcess with injected EventEmitter child and UTF-8 PassThrough, feed one valid near-limit line in fixed 1 KiB chunks, instrument searched-character counts in an isolated VM or measure sequentially with coordinator permission. Check identical notifications and errors.
findings.smallestFix: Track the already-searched prefix offset between chunks or collect segments until newline, preserving the existing bound and exact ordering. Require measured benefit before replacing parser.

findings.hypothesis: GitHub JSON response length is also checked after response.text has fully buffered the body.
findings.whyReachable: Release, metadata and comparison fetches share githubJSON; no streaming byte bound is applied before full text read.
findings.expectedScope: Updater check with anomalously large successful response. Static hypothesis only; no updater method invoked. Ordinary release response sizes not measured.
findings.risk: Updater changes require separate approval by coordinator, existing security checks and startup/rollback coverage. This review makes no updater behavior changes.
findings.cheapReproduction: Next test only: inject a fetcher returning a synthetic streaming Response into githubJSON and count bytes consumed before rejection. Do not call checkRelease or use real URLs/config.
findings.smallestFix: Consider a bounded body reader only after a separate updater review; preserve checksum, source ancestry, identity/signature checks and handoff rules.

excludedIdeas: Existing native decoder allocation/copy fix, page-context/translation weak retention and sidebar route pruning are prior verified work, not new findings.
Lazy folder child creation was rejected for slower opening; do not reintroduce it.
Disabling preflight, permissions, provider isolation, validation, checksum or signature checks is excluded.
Discovery catalog/status promises and up to 100 bounded history entries serve live functionality. No evidence that removing or caching across incompatible models is safe.
Host tool pending entries expire and are rejected on completion/cancel. No permanent map leak established.
Claude round listeners/timer have explicit cleanup; per-chat temporary dirs and process have finally cleanup. Native sidebar uses a weak callback. No leak proved there.
Updater streams its DMG with pipeline backpressure and validates byte count/hash. Its 500ms process polling is bounded, active-update-only and necessary for safe replacement.
Eager static updater/Organato imports impose bounded startup cost; no measurement justifies a lazy-import refactor.
Organato list retains full objects for at most 10 accepted pages before projecting display fields. Earlier projection might save bounded memory but no representative payload measured.
contextParts serializes before slicing to 180000 characters; native frame size bounds source data. No real large-context workload measured.
No end-to-end efficiency claims, no production fixes, installation, app launch, PC access or timings.
